sections.title: Front matter

sections.title: Historical background.
sections.extract: Carl Friedrich Gauss, in a half-page paper dated January 22, 1833, gave an integral formula for the linking number of two disjoint smooth closed curves in Euclidean 3-space: Lk(K1, K2) = 1/(4π) ∫K1×K2 dx/ds × dy/dt ∙ (x — y)/|x — y|3 ds dt . sections.title: Organization of this report.
sections.extract: Gauss's degree-of-map derivation of his linking integral does not work on the 3-sphere S3 because the set of ordered pairs of distinct points in S3 deformation retracts to a 3-sphere rather than to a 2-sphere, as it does in R3 . sections.title: Maxwell's equations on S3 and H3 .
sections.extract: Maxwell's equations, so familiar to us in Euclidean 3-space R3 , can also be shown to hold on S3 and H3 , with the appropriate definitions, as follows. Let ρ be a smooth real-valued function, which we think of as a charge density. On R3 and H3 , we ask that ρ have compact support, while on S3 we ask that it have average value zero. sections.extract: We follow Calugareanu's lead and replace the two closed curves K1 and K2 in our linking integrals by a single closed curve K , which we must assume to be simple. sections.title: Helicity of vector fields on S3 and H3 .
sections.extract: If V is a smooth vector field on R3 with compact support, then the Woltjer- Moffatt formula for its helicity, H(V) = 1/(4π) ∫ R3 × R3 V(x) × V(y) ∙ (x — y)/|x — y|3 dx dy , can be written succinctly as H(V) = ∫ R3 BS(V)(y) ∙ V(y) dy . sections.extract: Let Ω be a compact, smoothly bounded subdomain of R3 , S3 or H3 , and V a smooth vector field defined on Ω . sections.title: Spectral geometry of the curl operator in R3 , S3 and H3 .
sections.extract: Again let Ω be a compact, smoothly bounded subdomain of R3 , S3 or H3 . We are interested here in curl eigenfields on Ω , that is, vector fields V on Ω which satisfy ∇ × V = λ V , for λ ≠ 0 . In R3 these eigenfields are used to model stable plasma flows; see our paper (1999). Curl eigenfields exist for every value of λ . For example, in R3 , if V = sin λz i + cos λz j , then ∇ × V = λ V .
